newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian, foreign investors launch $35 mln hotel.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian, foreign investors launch $35 mln hotel.

text.p: Jordanian and foreign investors led by Arab Jordan Invesment Bank launched on Thursday a 15 million dinar ($21 million) tourism firm to develop the country's first Four Seasons hotel, investors said.
Hani al-Qadi, managing director of the newly set-up Mediterranean Tourism Investment Company said the board was elected on Thursday.
"We are now moving into the development stage of the hotel," said Qadi, adding that the estimated construction cost of the five-star Four Seasons hotel was around 25 million dinars.
The major investors in the new tourism company are Amman-based Arab Jordan Investment Bank and its associate firm Arab Jordan Investment Company, holding nearly 44 percent of its paid up capital.

Qadi said the remaining shares are held by foreign investors led by Saudi Arabian billionare Prince Al-Walid bin-Talal who has a 20 percent holding while the Toronto-based Four Seasons has acquired a 5 percent stake in the hotel it will manage.
This is the first Jordanian investment by the Saudi prince who visited recently the kingdom and showed interest in investing in the tourism and communications sectors.
Other individual Arab investors hold small holdings.
Four Seasons, which sold 25 percent of the company to the Saudi prince in 1995, has already announced plans for a series of hotels in the Middle East.

The 175-room five star hotel will be Amman's most luxurious to cater for higher end business vistors and tourists, Qadi said adding the hotel would cater for a forecast growth in demand for rooms by the year 2000.
Qadi said the hotel was expected to open within three years at a prime site in the capital Amman. Construction is due to start end of 1997 after completion of the design stage.
